newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr National says open to takeover - paper.
newsitem.headline: Cr National says open to takeover - paper.

text.p: French bank Credit National, which has been declaring for some time that its share is undervalued, believes it is open to takeover, chairman Emmanuel Rodocanachi said in an interview to appear in Le Journal des Finances.
"Credit National is without a doubt a tempting target," he said in the interview to be published in the weekly's Saturday edition. An advance copy was supplied to Reuters.

Rodocanachi, who has made similar comments to Reuters and others recently, said his group's share was undervalued and that the market had underestimated the potential of its acquisition of BFCE bank, which is in the process of integrating.
Credit National's share closed up 2.07 percent at 291.40 francs on Friday. Its year high is 423.0 and year low 226.0 francs.

IBCA rating agency said on November 5 it was downgrading Credit National's short term notes to A and A- from A1 and A2 and its long term notes to A- from A on the grounds that the bank's profitability should hit a low in 1996 because of exceptional charges for restructuring.
He said recently the group's net asset value would be around 600 francs a share without taking account of latent capital gains value.
